To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean dipole moment of the methyl group in CH3NC is 0.35 e, which is between the corresponding mean dipole moments in CH3F (0.54 e) and CH3CN (0.11 e).
The molecular force field of CH3NC is obtained from its gas phase IR spectrum.

the mean dipole moment of CH3NC is 1.5 times that of CH3F, the mean dipole moments of the methyl carbons are CH3F < CH3CN < CH3NC, and the dipole moment of the terminal carbon in CH3CN is 1.4 times that of CH2F2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the infrared fundamental intensities, molecular force field and principal component graphical representations of methyl isocianide.
the determination of molecular properties from gas phase infrared spectra of CH3NC, CH3CN and CH3F.
the development of an accurate and efficient procedure to determine the infrared fundamental intensities of CH3NC and the molecular force field and dipole polar tensor elements of the molecule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CH3NC has a more polarizable methyl group than CH3CN and CH3F.

the polar tensor elements of CH3NC are similar to CH3CN, and that the methyl group polarizability tensor elements are similar to CH4, but the dipole moment derivative of the methyl carbon is similar to the terminal atom dipole moment derivatives of CH3X, X = CN and F.
the infrared fundamental intensity data and the molecular dipole moment derivatives of CH3NC are now well determined and understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the infrared fundamental intensities of CH3NC have been accurately determined and the molecular polar tensor elements have been determined for the first time.
the molecular force field and infrared fundamental intensities of CH3NC are now known to an accuracy of better than 1% in most cases.

the molecular force field of methyl isocynide has been determined from its fundamental frequencies and infrared intensites, and the signs of dipole moment derivatives have been established from ab initio calculations and the infrared intensities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the infrared intensities and dipole moment derivatives are sensitive to the choice of the basis set.
it is possible to determine a molecular polar tensor and force field from infrared intensities alone.
the infrared intensity data of methyl isocianide are consistent with a planar geometry.
